text: Copper displaces metals below it. In silver nitrate it grows a glittering silver tree, and the solution turns blue. And here is a trap. Copper dissolves in iron three chloride, even though iron is above copper. That is because the couple involved is iron three over iron two, at plus zero point seven seven volts, which sits above copper. This reaction etches printed circuit boards.
